corrections.claim: Finite raw zero amplitudes directly equal local Euler coefficients.
corrections.result: At a=1/400 and u=log2, the prime contribution is about 1.40e-36 but the zero sum is about -0.736822760644. Pole and gamma terms explain the difference. Smoothing leakage also separates the prime sum from an individual coefficient.

corrections.claim: Unknown-zero tails require assuming all unknown zeros are on the critical line.
corrections.result: For these Gaussian tests, the positive moment at s=2 bounds unknown zeros using only 0<Re(rho)<1. This does not establish global GRH.

corrections.claim: Two higher-precision arithmetic runs remove uncertainty in inherited root brackets.
corrections.result: Both runs reuse the same finite root intervals. Their uncertainty dominates the final residual width; new root refinement is required to reduce it.

corrections.claim: Fixed finite height supports the limit of arbitrarily narrow arithmetic smoothing.
corrections.result: The bound requires a*(4+T^2)>=1 and explicit tail/precision control. A joint height-width-precision budget is a remaining gate.

corrections.claim: The alternate digamma integral needs no elementary gamma normalization.
corrections.result: The -4 log(2 pi) g(0) term is necessary; the zero-frequency control rejected its initial omission.
